title: Rockstar 的 GTA 手游收入突破 9500 万美元，免费游玩竞品涌现
content:
Rockstar’s GTA games pass $95m on mobile as free-to-play contenders emerge – Mobilegamer.biz
Skip to content
With GTA 6 launching tomorrow (November 19), we’ve looked at Rockstar’s own games and the wider ‘GTA-alike’ category on mobile to see which other studios are trying to ride the hype wave.
Rockstar’s mobile games
AppMagic
estimates suggest Rockstar has earned $109m in combined lifetime revenue from the iOS and Android editions of its games, with the GTA series accounting for $95.5m of that. These figures stretch back to 2010 for Chinatown Wars, so that’s well over a decade of cumulative earnings.
Here are each game’s estimated lifetime revenue and download figures, according to
AppMagic
:
Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
: $56m revenue, 7.9m downloads
GTA: Vice City – Definitive
: $16.6m revenue, 12.5m downloads
Bully: Anniversary Edition
: $8.8m revenue, 10.8m downloads
Grand Theft Auto III
: $7.5m revenue, 1.3m downloads
GTA: Liberty City Stories:
$5m revenue, 42m downloads
Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy
: $4.4m revenue, 315k downloads
GTA: Chinatown Wars
: $3.7m revenue, 16.5m downloads
Max Payne Mobile
: $2.3m revenue, 669k downloads
GTA: San Andreas – Definitive
: $1.9m revenue, 209k downloads
Red Dead Redemption
: $1.1m revenue, 74k downloads
GTA III – Definitive:
$477k revenue, 3.5m downloads
Rockstar’s total earnings from GTA on mobile are actually likely to be much higher overall thanks to its
deal with Netflix
, which saw the remastered PS2 GTA trilogy arrive on the streaming service back in 2023. Unconfirmed industry rumours around this deal suggest that this figure could have been as much as $50m.
Famously, Rockstar and Netflix partnered to reveal the first gameplay footage of GTA VI this summer.
Because the mobile GTAs are premium, these revenue numbers are naturally way below what a large-scale, big-brand free to play game typically earns. So there are plenty of other contenders out there, both live on the store now and incoming, that are looking to take a slice of the same market.
NTE: Neverness to Everness (Hotta Studio)
Known to many online as “anime GTA”, Neverness to Everness has generated around $46.4m on mobile since its global launch on April 24, 2026, AppMagic estimates. It has been downloaded around 12.2m times, with Japan (33%) and China (26%) as its biggest markets for revenue. Across all platforms, Perfect World put NTE’s lifetime revenue at $298m in its
first-half results
.
Developer Hotta is the team behind open world RPG Tower of Fantasy, and NTE is published by Perfect World Games. It’s now available on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. This week it was named best cross-device game in many Asian markets in
Google Play’s Best of 2026 awards
, and it’s up for best mobile game at
The Game Awards
on December 10.
OneState RP: Role Play Online (Chillbase)
Chillbase’s GTA-like released in April 2022, and has quietly earned an estimated $90.2m since, with 43% of those earnings from players in the US. That’s not far off the GTA series’ combined mobile total. AppMagic says it has racked up 61.7m downloads to date, with Brazil (18%) the top market.
It’s currently the top search ad on the App Store when you search “GTA”.
Gangstar Mirage City (Tencent)
Gangstar Mirage City, a GTA/Cyberpunk-like hybrid published by Tencent’s Level Infinite and officially licensed from Gameloft,
left its Philippines soft launch on August 20
. It rolled out across Latin America, the Middle East and North Africa, South Asia, Eastern and Central Europe and Southeast Asia, but not Western Europe or North America.
Still listed on AppMagic under its old name, Codename Crime-Vice Open World, it has made around $1.25m from 16.7m downloads to date. Malaysia (27%) is its biggest revenue market, and India (25%) is its biggest download market. If Tencent backs a wider launch, it could pose a significant threat to Take-Two’s official offerings.
Gangstar Vegas (Gameloft)
Gangstar Vegas is the oldest game on this list. Released in 2013 and developed by Gameloft Montreal, it is estimated to have clocked up 201m lifetime downloads and $28m lifetime revenue.
It still has a strong presence in GTA-related searches on the App Store, but made only about $41k from IAPs in the last 30 days.
The GTA-likes in soft launch
Garena Free City (Garena)
From the minds behind the monster battle royale Free Fire, this one first appeared in soft launch nearly two years ago on Android in Argentina, then expanded to the Philippines, Algeria, Egypt, and other smaller markets.
It has pulled in 1.4m downloads so far, but has made just $41.7k, AppMagic estimates, with 78% of that from the Philippines. Garena is an experienced mobile game-maker and has obviously had huge success with Free Fire, so if this makes it out of soft launch, it could be a real contender.
Pure Crime: Gangster City (Miniclip)
Miniclip’s Derby studio is behind this one, another GTA-like title under the Tencent umbrella that seems to take more cues from the PS2-era titles.
Now renamed Pure Crime: Gangster City RP, it quietly entered soft launch in the UK and the Philippines in summer 2025, says AppMagic, but it still isn’t generating meaningful revenue: just $2.7k to date from 567k downloads, mostly in the Philippines.
